title: What If America Had Adopted Hippo Meat? — Replacement Opening

worlds.base_prompt: Premium editorial illustrated-history visual essay with cinematic depth and tactile detail. Alternate materially different wide, medium, close, macro, overhead, over-shoulder, diagram and reaction compositions. Every new noun, action, place, joke or historical turn gets a genuinely new master image; never disguise a repeated composition as a crop.

narration.narration: This burger almost wasn't beef. In another America, the family cookout, the grocery aisle, even the diner special could have meant one enormous thing: hippo.
The strange part is this wasn't a joke. In 1910, meat prices were a political problem, and Americans were hunting for a new source of cheap protein.
One proposal sounded impossible: bring hippopotamuses to Louisiana, let them eat invasive water plants, then turn the animals themselves into dinner.
Now picture the plan actually working. Bayous become hippo ranches. Butchers learn a whole new animal. Menus stop looking strange because hippo becomes normal.
It never became the American dinner table. But that ordinary burger is now a reminder: history isn't only what happened. It's also the weird futures we barely avoided.
